Tosafot on Bava Batra 135a:11:1.hebrew: אביי אמר לעולם חייב - וקשה: דרב יהודה אדרב יהודה! דבריש שור שנגח את הפרה (ב"ק דף מו. ושם) אמר רב יהודה אמר שמואל: זו דברי סומכוס, אבל חכמים אומרים: זה כלל גדול בדין, המע"ה. ומפרש התם דזה כלל גדול: אפי' ניזק אומר ברי ומזיק אומר שמא. אלמא לרב יהודה ברי ושמא לאו ברי עדיף. וי"ל: דוקא גבי מלוה אית ליה לרב יהודה דברי עדיף, דהוי ברי חשוב; דאם לא הלוהו לא היה מעיז פניו לומר "מנה לי בידך", שהרי הלוה יודע שלא הלוה ממנו כלום, ושמא של לוה גרוע, שהיה לו לידע אם הלוה או לא הלוה, ולכך חייב. אבל גבי שור שנגח את הפרה דלא חשיב ברי של ניזק, משום דיודע שהמזיק אינו יודע מתי ילדה, קודם נגיחה או לאחר נגיחה, לכך טוען ברי, שיודע שלא יכחישנו המזיק; ושמא של מזיק אינו גרוע, כי אין לו לידע, כי לא היה שם. אבל קשה הא דאמר בפ"ק דכתובות (דף יב: ושם): אמר ליה אביי לרב יוסף: הא דרב יהודה, אמר "מנה לי בידך" והלה אומר "איני יודע" חייב, דשמואל היא, דפסיק התם כרבן גמליאל דנאמנת כשאמרה "משארסתני נאנסתי", ו"נסתחפה שדהו". והשתא הא אפילו רב יהודה מודה לשם דאינה נאמנת, לפי שהבעל אינו יודע מתי נאנסה, לא חשיב ברי שלה, כי ההיא דניזק ומזיק (ומיהו י"ל דהוה מצי למימר וליטעמיך). וכן בריש הבית והעלייה (ב"מ דף קטז: ושם) גבי "אם היה מכיר מקצת אבניו נוטלן", ומוקי לה דקאמר "איני יודע", וקאמר: לימא תיהוי תיובתא דר"נ ור' יוחנן דאמרי: "מנה לי בידך" והלה אומר "איני יודע" פטור? והשתא הא לרב יהודה נמי הוי תיובתא, דמודה התם דפטור, דהוי ברי גרוע, משום דאידך אינו יודע אם היו שלו, לפי שהרבה אבנים דומות זו לזו. וי"ל: דאביי דהכא לא משוי חילוק בין ברי חשוב דמלוה לברי גרוע, דהא קאמר הכא "לעולם חייב". ושאני הכא, דכי "מנה לאחר בידך" דמי; משמע דאם הוא עצמו היה אומר "אחיך אני" והוא אומר "איני יודע", יטול בחלקו, אע"ג דהוי ברי גרוע, דהם אינן יודעים אם יש להם אח במדינת הים או לאו. והשתא אתי שפיר דההיא דכתובות אביי אמר לה, וההיא דהבית והעלייה (שם) נמי דקאמר "לימא תהוי תיובתא דר"נ", משום דלאביי לא הוי תיובתא דרב יהודה. ו"זה כלל גדול בדין" דריש פרק הפרה — לא מוקי אביי לאיתויי אפילו ניזק אומר ברי ומזיק אומר שמא, אלא מוקי להכי דאמר התם. א"נ לכי הא דאיתמר (לעיל בבא בתרא דף צב.): המוכר שור לחבירו ונמצא נגחן, דאזלינן בתר חזקה אפילו כנגד רובא. ואין להאריך כאן:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 135a:11:1.english: Abaye said: Actually, he is liable - And this is difficult: Rav Yehuda [here] contradicts Rav Yehuda [elsewhere]! For at the beginning of [the chapter] "Shor She-Nagach et ha-Parah" (Bava Kamma 46a, and there) Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel: These are the words of Sumchus, but the Sages say: This is a great principle in law — the burden of proof rests upon the one who seeks to extract [money] from his fellow. And there it is explained that this "great principle" applies even if the damaged party says "I am certain" and the damager says "perhaps." Thus, according to Rav Yehuda, a claim of "certain" against a claim of "perhaps" is not preferred. And one can answer: Rav Yehuda holds that a "certain" claim is preferred only in the case of a loan, since it is a significant certainty; for had he not lent him, he would not brazenly say, "I have a maneh [owed] by you," because the borrower knows that he borrowed nothing from him. And the "perhaps" of the borrower is weak, since he should know whether he borrowed or did not borrow, and therefore he is liable. But in the case of an ox that gored a cow, the damaged party's certainty is not considered significant, because he knows that the damager does not know when [the cow] gave birth — before the goring or after the goring. Therefore he claims "certain," because he knows the damager will not contradict him; and the "perhaps" of the damager is not weak, since he has no way of knowing, as he was not there. But there is a difficulty with what is said in the first chapter of Ketubot (12b, and there): Abaye said to Rav Yosef: That statement of Rav Yehuda — [if one] says "I have a maneh [owed] by you" and the other says "I don't know," he is liable — is [the view of] Shmuel, who rules there like Rabban Gamliel, that she is believed when she says, "Since you betrothed me, I was raped," and "his field was swept away." But now, even Rav Yehuda concedes there that she is not believed, because the husband does not know when she was raped; her certainty is not considered significant, like that of the damaged party and the damager. (However, one can say that [Abaye] could have said [to Rav Yosef], "And according to your own reasoning...") And likewise at the beginning of [the chapter] "Ha-Bayit ve-ha-Aliyah" (Bava Metzia 116b, and there), regarding "If he recognized some of its stones, he takes them": it establishes this [as a case] where he says "I don't know," and [the Gemara] asks: Shall we say this is a refutation of Rav Nachman and Rabbi Yochanan, who say that [if one says] "I have a maneh [owed] by you" and the other says "I don't know," he is exempt? But now, this would be a refutation for Rav Yehuda as well, for he concedes there that [the defendant] is exempt, since it is a weak certainty, because the other does not know whether the stones were his, as many stones resemble one another. And one can answer: Abaye here does not make a distinction between the significant certainty of a loan and a weak certainty, for he says here, "Actually, he is liable." But here it is different, for it is like [a claim that] "a maneh of another is in your hand." This implies that if he himself were saying, "I am your brother," and the other said, "I don't know," he would take his share, even though it is a weak certainty, since they do not know whether they have a brother overseas or not. And now it is well explained that the passage in Ketubot was said by Abaye; and also that [passage] in "Ha-Bayit ve-ha-Aliyah" (there), which says, "Shall we say this is a refutation of Rav Nachman," [phrased that way] because for Abaye it is not a refutation of Rav Yehuda. And as for "This is a great principle in law" at the beginning of the chapter "Ha-Parah" — Abaye does not establish it as including even [a case where] the damaged party says "certain" and the damager says "perhaps," but rather establishes it as [referring to] what is stated there. Alternatively, it is like that which was stated (above, Bava Batra 92a): One who sells an ox to his fellow and it is found to be a gorer — we follow the presumption even against the majority. And there is no need to elaborate here.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 135a:1:1.hebrew: חזיא לכהנא רבה - יש מוחקים "רבה", משום דלכל הפחות אלמנה היא, ולא חזיא לכהן גדול. ואומר ר"י דשפיר גרס "רבה", דהא אף לכהן הדיוט אסירא, דהא מטעם שאמר "גרשתיה" היה מתיר, ולא שהיה אומר שהיו לו בנים — דא"כ היה נאמן, כדתנן במתניתין: "זה בני" נאמן. ומאי הוי? מייתי עלה מילתא דר' יוחנן. אלא הכי פירושו: דחזיא לכהנא רבה, כלומר: אינה זקוקה ליבום, שגרשתיה דמותרת לכל העולם, ואפי' לכהן גדול, מטעם זיקת יבמין. וה"ר מנחם גרס "חזיא לכהונה", כלומר: אינה זקוקה ליבם, וחוזרת לכהונת בי נשא, לאכול בתרומה:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 135a:1:1.english: She is fit for the High Priest - Some delete the word "High," because at the very least she is a widow, and [a widow] is not fit for the High Priest. But Rabbi Yitzchak says that the reading "High" is correct, for even to an ordinary priest she is forbidden, since the reason he was permitting [her] was that he said "I divorced her," and not that he was saying that he had sons — for if so, he would be believed, as we learned in our Mishnah: [if he says] "This is my son," he is believed. And what would be [the point], seeing that [the Gemara] cites in connection with it a statement of Rabbi Yochanan? Rather, this is its explanation: that she is fit for the High Priest, meaning: she is not bound to levirate marriage, since [he said] "I divorced her," so that she is permitted to everyone, even to a High Priest, because of the levirate bond. And Rabbeinu Menachem reads "she is fit for the priesthood," meaning: she is not bound to a levir, and she returns to the priesthood of her father's house, to eat terumah.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 135a:4:1.hebrew: ה"ג הא אמרי דאיכא סהדי במדינת הים דידעי דאית ליה אחי - וה"פ: הא יצא קול הכא שאומרים דאיכא עדים במדינת הים. ול"ג "והא איכא סהדי במדינת הים", דאי ודאי דאיכא עדים במדינת הים, א"כ מאי קאמר "השתא מיהא הא ליתנהו"? ואי בעי למימר שיש לנו לחוש שמא יש עדים — הא ודאי ליכא למיחש, דהא תנן "יש לי בנים" נאמן, וה"ה "אין לי אחים" נאמן, דמגו דאי בעי פטר לה בגיטא. וכן בפרק שני דכתובות (דף כג. ושם) על בנתיה דמר שמואל דאישתביין, ופריך: "הא אמרי איכא עדים במדינת הים". אבל אי ליכא קול, אין לנו לחוש מאלינו שמא יש עדים, דהא תנן התם: "נשביתי וטהורה אני" נאמנת:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 135a:4:1.english: This is how we read it: "But they say that there are witnesses overseas who know that he has brothers" - And this is its meaning: A rumor has gone out here, as people are saying that there are witnesses overseas. And we do not read, "But there are witnesses overseas," for if it were certain that there are witnesses overseas, then what is [Rava] saying, "Now, in any case, they are not here"? And if he wanted to say that we must be concerned that perhaps there are witnesses — surely there is no need to be concerned, for we learned in a Mishnah that if a man says, "I have sons," he is believed, and the same applies [if he says], "I have no brothers," he is believed, since [he has] a *migo*: had he wanted, he could have exempted her [from levirate marriage] with a bill of divorce. And so too in the second chapter of Ketubot (23a, there), regarding the daughters of Mar Shmuel who were taken captive, and [the Gemara] asks: "But they say that there are witnesses overseas." But if there is no rumor, we need not be concerned on our own that perhaps there are witnesses, for we learned there in the Mishnah: "I was taken captive, and I am pure" — she is believed.
